semantically_equivalent_models.justification: The 'bert-based dense retriever' is built upon the BERT model, making 'bert' semantically equivalent because it is the foundational model for the retriever.
'bert-base' is a smaller version of BERT that can directly serve as the base model for a 'bert-based dense retriever', making it semantically equivalent.

parent_models.justification: Since 'bert-based dense retriever' uses BERT as its foundation, 'bert-base' is a more general model as it encompasses all models derived from BERT, including BERT-based retrievers.
'bert' is a more general model than 'bert-based dense retriever' as it is the architecture from which the retriever is developed, making it a parent model.
'Dense retrievers' can be seen as specialized forms of dense architectures, thus making 'dense neural networks' a broad parent category.
The 'bert-based dense retriever' falls under the category of 'large language models' as BERT itself is a large language model, which can be used in various applications including retrieval.

closest_parent_model.justification: 'bert' serves as the immediate foundational parent for the 'bert-based dense retriever' as it directly leverages the BERT architecture, making it the closest parent model.

child_models.justification: This model is a specialized form of 'bert-based dense retriever', enhancing it with multilingual capabilities, thus making it a child model.

closest_child_model.justification: The 'multilingual dense passage retriever' is directly built upon the framework of 'bert-based dense retriever' with added multilingual capabilities, making it the closest child model.

sibling_models.justification: 'transformer-bert' is another derivative of BERT, similar in semantic space to 'bert-based dense retriever' since both are based on the BERT architecture.
'concept-bert' is a model variation deriving from BERT, making it a sibling within the BERT family of models.
As a model based on BERT, 'bertoverflow' fits into the same family of adaptations and applications of BERT, hence qualifying it as a sibling model.
'bertsumext' is another model built upon BERT for summarization tasks, sharing the same parent and fitting as a sibling model.

closest_sibling_model.justification: 'transformer-bert' is likely to be the closest sibling as both models emphasize similar transformer-based architecture and capabilities derived directly from BERT.

unrelated_models.justification: 'lambdamart' is a learning-to-rank framework based on boosting trees, unrelated to 'bert-based dense retriever'.
An 'autoencoder' model focusing on encoding input into a compact representation is unrelated to BERT-based dense retrieval mechanisms.
